Spawn, edit, view, and validate typed instances through hand-rolled UIs with zero plugin dependencies. ## Key features * **One tiddler per type** -- the type's full schema lives in fields and a JSON-encoded `kind.fields` array on a single tiddler. Body stays free for prose documentation. * **Namespaces** -- types declare `kind.namespaces` (multi-membership). A namespace switcher restricts what's visible to the active scope. * **Auto-computed titles** -- types declare a `kind.title-formula` filter; new instances get their title computed from sibling fields (e.g. `parent/abbrev`). * **Live validation + bulk validator** -- inline errors as you edit; wiki-wide scan report on the validator tab. * **Typeahead refs** -- filterable search input + filtered dropdown + selected pills with × remove; scales to large option sets. * **Configurable stream-river view** -- each type chooses which fields appear in its in-river field bar; empty = bar hidden. * **Hand-rolled UI** -- zero dependency on other rimir plugins (theme/components/typed). Optional soft dependency on doc-template for the branded documentation hub. ## Prerequisites No external prerequisites. Optional: `rimir/doc-template` for the documentation hub. ## Quick start 1. Open the **type-builder** tab and define a new type (key, caption, icon, namespaces, title-formula, fields). 2. Open the **creator** tab, pick the type, fill the fields, click Create. 3. Open the resulting tiddler in the story river — the stream-view field bar appears at the top. 4. Use the **validator** tab for a wiki-wide constraint scan. ## Plugin Library This plugin is part of the [rimir-cc tw-plugin-library](https://rimir-cc.github.io/tw-plugin-library/). Schema model |!Element |!Stored as |!Discovery | |Type |One tiddler with fields `kind.type`, `kind.caption`, `kind.icon`, `kind.namespaces`, `kind.title-formula`, `kind.stream-fields`, `kind.fields` (JSON) |`[has[kind.type]has[kind.fields]]` | |Field def |Entry inside the type's `kind.fields` JSON array |`[get[kind.fields]jsonindexes[]]` | |Instance |Any tiddler with `kind.type: ` |`[kind.type]` | There are no separate per-field tiddlers, no inheritance slots, no enum tiddlers. The type tiddler is the single source of truth for its schema. !! Namespace mechanism * Each type's `kind.namespaces` field is a space-separated list of namespace tokens — a type can belong to many at once. * The active namespace lives in `$:/config/rimir/kind/active-namespace` (single value; empty = all). * All UI surfaces that enumerate types — //creator//, //overview//, //validator// — filter via the `kind.belongs-to-ns` function in `engine.tid`. !! Field types (`typed` values) |!`typed` |!Editor |!Storage | |`text` |single-line `<$edit-text>` |plain string | |`longtext` |textarea |plain string | |`number` |numeric input |plain string | |`date` |`<$edit-date>` |TW date format | |`datetime` |`<$edit-date>` with time |TW datetime format | |`enum` |single: `<$select>`; multi: pill toggle row |single string or list-field | |`ref` |typeahead (filter input + dropdown + selected pills with ×) |single tiddler title or list-field | |`$title` |read-only |computed from `kind.title-formula` | |`$calculated` |read-only |computed from the field's `formula` | Extension point: `field-input.tid` is one `<%if [match[X]]%>` cascade. Adding a field type = one new branch. !! Constraints |!Constraint |!Meaning | |`required` |Must have a value (blocking) | |`min:N` |Min N characters (text/longtext) or N entries (multi-enum / multi-ref) | |`max:N` |Max N characters or entries | |`unique` |Unique among instances of the same type | |`unique:wiki` |Unique wiki-wide (across all tiddlers) | The validator reports any violation as a row in its bulk report. The editor shows live error messages below each input. !! Title generation When `kind.title-formula` is set, the creator computes a new instance's title by evaluating the formula against the draft state tiddler: ``` \function kind.eval-title(type-tid, target-tid) [get[kind.title-formula]] :map[subfilter] ``` Example formula: `[get[parent]][[/]][get[abbrev]]+[join[]]` produces `parent-title/abbrev` style titles. !! Stream-view (ViewTemplate auto-registration) `viewtemplate.tid` is tagged `$:/tags/ViewTemplate` with `list-after: $:/core/ui/ViewTemplate/title`. On any tiddler with a `kind.type` field, it renders `stream-view.tid`, which reads `kind.stream-fields` from the type and emits a compact bar. Empty/missing `kind.stream-fields` = bar renders nothing (self-disabling). A click on a field cell opens a popup containing the field's editor; a top-bar toggle switches to inline-edit mode (the editor replaces the cell directly). !! Shared infrastructure * ''engine.tid'' — all shared functions: type discovery, namespace filtering, JSON field-array accessors, constraint extraction, validation predicates, display helpers (truncation, ref resolution), title-formula evaluation * ''field-input.tid'' — typed-dispatch input widget used by editor, stream-view popup, stream-view inline, and type-builder live preview * ''editor.tid'' — 2-column table editor; takes only `target-tid` in scope; transcludes field-input per row "},"$:/plugins/rimir/kind/doc/dev-workflow":{"title":"$:/plugins/rimir/kind/doc/dev-workflow","rdt.order":"3","rdt.plugin-key":"kind","rdt.plugin-name":"kind","rdt.plugin-subtitle":"Lightweight schema engine — one tiddler per type, namespaced","rdt.section":"Dev Workflow","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"<$transclude $tiddler="$:/plugins/rimir/doc-template/templates/page"> <$fill $name="body"> !! Defining a new type # Open the //type-builder// tab (`$:/plugins/rimir/kind/type-builder`). # Use the ''Create blank type'' button, supplying a new title (e.g. `$:/myns/types/task`). # Fill the metadata section: `kind.type` (key), `kind.caption`, `kind.icon`, `kind.namespaces`, `kind.title-formula`, `kind.stream-fields`. # Edit the JSON in the //Field definitions// section. The //Parsed preview// table updates as you type; the //Live editor preview// shows what an instance editor will look like. # Open the //creator// tab and try creating an instance. !! Adding a new field type # Open `field-input.tid`. # Find the dispatch cascade (`<%elseif [match[X]]%>` chain). # Add a new branch for your new `typed` value. # (Optional) Update the //typed// reference table in `doc/architecture.tid`. !! Adding a new constraint # Open `engine.tid`. # Add a `kind.viol-(type-tid, field-key, target-tid)` filter function that returns non-empty when the constraint is violated. # Add a corresponding `<%if [function[kind.viol-]]%>` branch in `field-input.tid` (for live errors) and `validator.tid` (for bulk report). # Extend `kind.viol-any` so the creator's disabled-button predicate covers the new constraint. !! Known limitations (v0.1.0) * The type-builder's field-list editor is a textarea (raw JSON); a fully-structured row-by-row editor with add/delete/reorder is planned for v0.2. * Multi-value uniqueness is exact-string-equality, not set-equality. Two instances with assignees `"alice bob"` and `"bob alice"` are NOT considered duplicates. * No referential integrity: deleting a tiddler that other instances reference does not clean up the references. * No schema migration: changing a field's `typed` after instances exist may leave stale values. Filling fields and clicking Create produces a tiddler titled `/` with `kind.type: task` and the field values written through. !! A shared "note" type (orga and private namespaces) A type can belong to multiple namespaces: ``` title: $:/shared/types/note kind.type: note kind.namespaces: orga private kind.caption: Note kind.icon: 📝 kind.title-formula: [[note-]] [get[topic]] +[join[]] kind.stream-fields: topic created kind.fields: [{"key":"topic","caption":"Topic","typed":"text","constraints":["required"]},{"key":"body","caption":"Body","typed":"longtext"}] ``` Switching the active namespace between ''orga'' and ''private'' (in //settings//) — this type appears in both. !! Multi-ref typeahead (large option sets) For ref fields with many possible targets, the typeahead UI shows a filterable search input. Selected values render as pills with × removal. Example field def: ```json {"key":"stakeholders","caption":"Stakeholders","icon":"👥","typed":"ref","ref-types":["person","team"],"cardinality":"multi"} ``` The candidate set is `[enlist[person team]] :map:flat[all[shadows+tiddlers]kind.type] +[unique[]]` — every instance of `person` or `team` in the wiki. The search input filters by title and caption. !! Validator interpretation Open the //validator// tab. Each type heading shows the instance count. A table follows with one row per violation: * ''Red rows'' — blocking constraints (`required`, `min:N`, `max:N`, `unique`, `unique:wiki`, title mismatch) If a type has no violations, the table is empty (just the heading + "//No instances//" if applicable). !! Q: Why a new plugin alongside `rimir/typed`? `typed` (~1600 lines) grew several features that don't pay rent inside TiddlyWiki's bag-of-fields model: * 3-level slot inheritance (`:0`/`:1`/`:2`) — needs `rrfunc` because native `function[]` leaks; needs `$importvariables` for the parent chain; capped at 3 levels by TW issue #9647 * Separate per-field tiddlers (e.g. ~40 in `orga-data-model`) * Per-type field overrides via the `validity` field * Cross-plugin enum tiddlers with their own inheritance * Two object-ref editor modes (typeahead + pills) `kind` keeps the spirit (schema-as-tiddlers, JSON-friendly, validator) and drops all of the above. The result is ~50% the code with explicit namespace support added. !! Q: Why no inheritance? In real schemas the inheritance was mostly used for one thing: a shared base (`_node`) defining common fields like `title`, `caption`, `description`, `parent`. With flat schemas you copy those 4-5 fields into every type tiddler. That's <50 lines of JSON duplication across a 10-type domain model — cheap, especially when the type-builder makes copy-paste easy. The override pattern (subtype dropping a base field via `:0`) was clever but rare and often a smell. And `[has[kind.type]]` already gives you an "all instances" filter without needing a base type. !! Q: How do I share fields across types? You don't, structurally. You copy the field def into each type's `kind.fields` JSON. That's the price of KISS. If you find yourself maintaining the same 10-field block across 8 types, you can extract a shared `kind.fields` value into a config tiddler and reference it — but for v0.1.0 that's manual. !! Q: How do I migrate from `rimir/typed`? Both plugins can coexist (different field namespaces: `rrt.*` vs `kind.*`, different instance markers). To migrate one type at a time: # Read the typed type tiddler's `rrt.fields:0()`, `:1()`, `:2()` body # Look up each field's def in the corresponding `*-data-model` plugin # Compose a single `kind.fields` JSON array with the union # Move `validity`-restricted overrides into the relevant subtype's JSON directly # Update instance tiddlers from `rrt.type: X` to `kind.type: X` (one-line `$:/state/...` action filter) After migrating all types, you can remove the typed plugin. !! Q: What if I want a field type that's not in the list? Add it. Open `field-input.tid`, find the `<%elseif [match[X]]%>` cascade, add a new branch. Whatever wikitext renders an editable widget. The constraint and validation logic in `engine.tid` already covers the generic cases (required/min/max/unique); add a `kind.viol-` function if your new type needs new constraints. !! Q: Why JSON for the field array instead of separate field tiddlers? The JSON-in-one-field approach trades reusability for locality. The whole schema for one type is in one tiddler — open it, see everything. With separate field tiddlers you'd be reading two or three tiddlers in parallel to understand a type. For the volume most users hit (single-digit types per namespace, 5-15 fields per type), locality wins. The `kind.fields` field stores stringified-JSON because storing as a `application/json` body would force the type tiddler to be saved as `.json + .json.meta` (two files), which breaks the convention of one-tiddler-per-file. The body stays free for prose documentation of the type. !! Q: Why aren't multi-value uniqueness checks set-aware? `unique` and `unique:wiki` use exact string equality on the whole field value. For multi-value refs/enums where order doesn't semantically matter (e.g. `assignee: "alice bob"` vs `assignee: "bob alice"`), this means a logical-duplicate isn't flagged. Fixing this properly would require value normalization (sort + dedupe before comparison) and a stronger uniqueness predicate. Planned for v0.2 if needed. What it does ''kind'' is a lightweight schema engine for TiddlyWiki. Each type's full definition — fields, constraints, title formula, icon, namespace memberships, and stream-river display config — lives on a single tiddler. Instances are plain tiddlers marked with a `kind.type` field. No inheritance, no separate per-field tiddlers, no central registry. !! Features * ''Schema-as-tiddler'' — one tiddler per type, with field defs as a JSON array in `kind.fields` * ''Discovery'' — `[all[shadows+tiddlers]has[kind.type]has[kind.fields]]` finds all type tiddlers * ''Namespaces'' — types declare `kind.namespaces`, the active scope picks one (or all) * ''Editor'' — 2-column form (label + input), table-style, with live validation messages * ''Field Bar'' — auto-rendered in the stream river on every instance; configurable per type; self-disabling * ''Creator'' — pick a type, fill fields, click Create; title computed from `kind.title-formula` * ''Validator'' — wiki-wide report of constraint violations * ''Type-builder'' — structured editor for type metadata + JSON textarea for fields, with live preview !! Schema model * ''Type tiddlers'' — fields `kind.type` (the key), `kind.caption`, `kind.icon`, `kind.namespaces`, `kind.title-formula`, `kind.stream-fields`, and `kind.fields` (JSON array) * ''Field defs'' — entries inside the JSON array with `key`, `typed`, `caption`, `icon`, `constraints`, `options` (enum), `ref-types` + `cardinality` (ref) * ''Instance tiddlers'' — any tiddler with `kind.type: ` is an instance !! Prerequisites TiddlyWiki ≥ 5.4.0 in Node.js server mode. No other plugin dependencies. Optional: `$:/plugins/rimir/doc-template` for the documentation hub you're reading right now. !! Quick start # Open the ''type-builder'' tab; create a blank type and fill its metadata # Paste a field-list JSON (see the Examples section) # Open the ''creator'' tab, pick the type, fill the fields, click Create # Open the resulting tiddler in the story river — the field bar appears at the top # Use the ''validator'' tab to scan the whole wiki for constraint violations <$transclude $tiddler="$:/plugins/rimir/doc-template/templates/callout" type="info"> <$fill $name="body">''Why a new plugin alongside `rimir/typed`?'' typed has accumulated features (3-level inheritance, separate per-field tiddlers, two ref-editor modes, ~1600 lines). kind drops everything that doesn't pay rent in TiddlyWiki's bag-of-fields model and adds namespaces. See the FAQ for details. JSON-in-field via `jsonget` / `jsonindexes` The whole field-array lives in `kind.fields` as a stringified JSON. Read it with: ``` [get[kind.fields]] ← the JSON text [get[kind.fields]jsonindexes[]] ← top-level array indices "0","1",… [get[kind.fields]jsonget,[key]] ← scalar at path [idx].key [get[kind.fields]jsonindexes,[constraints]] ← inner-array indices for constraints [get[kind.fields]jsonget,[constraints],] ← one constraint string ``` The engine uses `multi-arg jsonget` (the form with comma-separated path arguments) consistently — chaining single-arg `jsonget` calls inside `:map` is a known TW gotcha that returns empty. See `[[tw-gotchas-filters#jsonget chained inside :map`]]. !! Discovery via `kind.type` + `kind.fields` `[has[kind.type]has[kind.fields]]` finds tiddlers that look like type definitions — they need both fields. The `kind.fields` requirement filters out instance tiddlers (which have `kind.type` but no `kind.fields`). `all[shadows+tiddlers]` is implicit in `engine.tid`'s `kind.types-all`; plugin-bundled types ARE shadows. !! ViewTemplate auto-registration `viewtemplate.tid` is tagged `$:/tags/ViewTemplate` with `list-after: $:/core/ui/ViewTemplate/title`. TiddlyWiki's ViewTemplate cascade renders all matching templates in order; ours runs right after the title, so the field bar appears at the very top of the body. The `<%if [has[kind.type]] %>` guard means the template is silently a no-op for non-instance tiddlers. !! Title-formula evaluation pattern `kind.eval-title` mirrors the pattern from `rimir/typed`: ``` \function kind.eval-title(type-tid, target-tid) [get[kind.title-formula]] ← gets the filter STRING :map[subfilter] ← runs filter against target ``` The `subfilter` form makes `` the input source to the filter, and `` (the formula string from the outer map iteration) supplies the filter string to run. ''Formula authoring note'': each top-level run inside the formula starts with the subfilter source (the target instance). So write `[get[parent]]` (operates on source) NOT `[get[parent]]` (would override the source with the OUTER renderer's currentTiddler). The first form gets the target's parent; the second gets whatever tiddler is currently rendering the validator/creator UI — almost never what you want. !! Live + bulk validation sharing predicates Both `field-input.tid` (editor) and `validator.tid` (bulk) use the same `kind.viol-*` functions from `engine.tid`. The same constraint logic gives identical results in both surfaces, avoiding the typed-plugin trap where editor and validator drift apart over time. The predicates are filter functions, so they participate in `:filter` / `<%if%>` predicates naturally and don't require JS. !! Why no `rrfunc` `rrfunc` exists in `rimir/typed` to defend against the inheritance slot pattern: `rrt.fields:1()` and `:2()` may legitimately not exist on a base type, and native `function[]` would leak input titles in that case. With flat schemas (no slot pattern), every function we call is guaranteed to be defined — native `function[]` is safe. `kind` ships zero JS modules in v0.1.0. !! Restricted-wiki considerations There are none. `kind` doesn't touch the `rimir/llm-connect` restricted-wiki sandbox; tools running in that sandbox can read instances via the standard `get` filter operator, but the kind editor/creator/validator UIs are not meant to render inside a restricted-wiki tool execution. If a future use case needs that, the editor would need to be self-contained (no `\import`) — see `[[tw-gotchas-plugin-quirks#`rimir/llm-connect` restricted wiki blocks `\import`]]`. !! TW 5.4.0 compatibility Variables avoid colon-named identifiers (which 5.4.0 parses as dynamic-arg macro calls — see `[[tw-gotchas-540-migration#`<>` parses as macro dynamic arg]]`). Config tiddlers omit `type: text/plain` to avoid the filesystem-adapter's `.txt + .txt.meta` split (see `[[feedback-tid-vs-txt-meta]]`). Spawn, edit, view, and validate typed instances through hand-rolled UIs with zero plugin dependencies. !! Key features * ''One tiddler per type'' — schema lives in fields and a JSON-encoded `kind.fields` array on a single tiddler; body stays free for prose documentation * ''Namespaces'' — types declare `kind.namespaces` (multi-membership); a namespace switcher scopes what's visible * ''Auto-computed titles'' — types declare a `kind.title-formula` filter; new instances get their title computed from sibling fields * ''Live + bulk validation'' — inline errors as you edit, plus a wiki-wide validator report * ''Typeahead refs'' — filterable text input + dropdown + selected pills with × remove; scales to large option sets * ''Configurable stream-river view'' — each type chooses which fields appear in its in-river field bar; empty = bar hidden * ''Hand-rolled UI'' — zero dependency on other rimir plugins (theme/components/typed) !! Prerequisites No external prerequisites. Optional: `$:/plugins/rimir/doc-template` for the branded documentation hub. !!
